correctness.rationale: Uniform rooted plane trees with n edges correspond bijectively to Dyck paths of semilength n. Twice total vertex depth minus n equals the contour area sum. Catalan first-return decomposition proves \(W=z/(1-4z)\); Lagrange inversion and \(z(B^r)'/\sqrt{1-4z}\) give each exact conditional mean. The ratio \(c(m,r+1)/c(m,r)\) is strictly increasing with m for \(r\ge2\); \(r=1\) uses \(c(m,1)=c(m,2)\), giving the strict decreasing regression and \(n/2\) first drop. Finite sums show covariance with all nonconstant increasing g is negative. Singular expansions yield the fixed-degree mean and covariance \(-2n+O(\sqrt n)\). The standalone verifier independently enumerated Dyck paths to size 9 and passed 32688 rational/combinatorial checks.

value.rationale: The local degree of a uniform plane-tree root and the global total path length are canonical structural statistics. The exact conditional mean and strict regression for every root degree, all increasing transformations, the \(n/2\) first-degree penalty, fixed-r linear correction, and \(-2n\) covariance scale provide a complete dependence-sign result plus quantitative structure. This is not merely a numerical moment or arbitrary parameter slice; no downstream theorem or stochastic dominance is asserted.
